key_insight: GazeRIB trains chest X-ray models by masking regions radiologists did not look at, while using complete images at inference. The study systematically tests how individual readers versus multi-reader panels affect this supervision; the provided abstract does not include the results.
problem_solved: Radiologist gaze can guide medical image learning, but it remains unclear how the choice and number of readers influence its usefulness.
method: Collect repeated gaze recordings from eight experts interpreting the same 80 chest X-rays.
Compare gaze guidance from individual readers and panels of three, five, and eight readers.
Evaluate 910 models across seven architectures and 10 random seeds, applying gaze-based masking during training only.
impact: The evaluation addresses a practical design choice for gaze-supervised medical AI: whose attention to use and how many experts to involve. Full-image inference requires no gaze input at deployment.
visual_elements: Training-to-inference diagram: gaze heatmap → masked training X-ray → full-image inference.

paper_title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
paper_authors: Nattakorn Kittisut, Roy M. Gabriel, Marly van Assen, Mohammadreza Zandehshahvar, Carlo N. De Cecco
